speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have been experiencing chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to begin our evaluation, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and have you noticed any blood in your stool or unintended weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Ulcerative Colitis). 

The clinical presentation of chronic diarrhea, lower abdominal pain relieved by defecation, mucus discharge, and a sensation of incomplete evacuation (tenesmus) is classic for Ulcerative Colitis. While the camping history suggests a possible infectious trigger (Campylobacter, Shigella, or Yersinia), the duration of four months and specific symptom profile strongly favor an inflammatory etiology. 

REQUEST TEST: Fecal Calprotectin, CBC, CMP, ESR, CRP, and Stool Culture.
REQUEST IMAGES: Colonoscopy_with_biopsy.
